acceptedAnswer.text: Simple calculators evaluate strictly left to right as you press keys — 2+3 is computed as soon as × is pressed (=5), then 5×4=20. Scientific calculators and algebra follow order of operations (PEMDAS) instead, which would give 2+(3×4)=14. Use our Scientific Calculator for expression-based PEMDAS evaluation.
It divides the number currently on screen by 100 — so 50 % becomes 0.5, ready to use in a further calculation (e.g. for "20 × 15 %" to find 15% of 20).

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between C and AC?

acceptedAnswer.text: C (Clear) resets only the number you're currently typing, keeping any pending operation and running total. AC (All Clear) resets everything back to zero, including memory-pending calculations (but not the M register).

mainEntity.name: Can I use negative numbers and decimals?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — use ± to flip the sign of the current entry, and the decimal point key for fractional values, exactly as on a physical calculator.
It uses IEEE 754 double-precision floating point (about 15–17 significant decimal digits) — the same standard used by virtually all calculators, spreadsheets and programming languages.

mainEntity.name: Does this online calculator have memory and history?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. MC, MR, M+ and M− give you a memory register shown as MEM, and the History tape lists your last 50 completed calculations. You can copy the history or print it.

mainEntity.name: How do I add or subtract a percentage on a calculator?

acceptedAnswer.text: Type the amount, press ×, type 100 plus or minus the percentage, then press % and =. For example 851 × 106 % = gives 902.06 (6% added) and 200 × 85 % = gives 170 (15% off).

mainEntity.name: What keyboard shortcuts does it support?

acceptedAnswer.text: Digits and the decimal point, + - * /, Enter or = for equals, % for percent, Backspace to delete a digit and Esc for all clear.
Computers store 0.1 and 0.2 in binary, so the raw sum is 0.30000000000000004. The display rounds to 12 significant digits, so you see 0.3.

mainEntity.name: What do the error messages mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: Error: undefined appears after dividing by zero, Error: div by 0 when you press 1/x on zero, and Error: negative when you take the square root of a negative number. Press AC to clear it.
